title: Marking end-to-end integration test (3 users × 3 objects)
description: Proves Foundry-style mandatory access control (subset / AND semantics) end-to-end through the real oss.ServiceImpl.ListObjects path with markings enforcement turned on via security.Engine.SetMarkingsEnabled. The 3-user × 3-object matrix is designed so that single-term overlap semantics alone (the should-terms Bleve clause synthesised by the US-051 auto-marking rule) is NOT sufficient — the third 'both required' object exposes the gap between 'overlap ≥ 1 marking' and 'user ⊇ object markings'. US-052 closes that gap with a post-Bleve verification pass that runs auth.EvaluateMarkings per row inside the service layer so rows whose `_markings` slice is not a subset of the caller's marking set are dropped before the page is returned.

reservedFields.source: pkg/index.BuildMapping hard-reserves this keyword field on every ObjectType index — pkg/security.MarkingField is the canonical constant and pkg/funnel.markingsField / pkg/index.MarkingsField stay in lockstep

engine.note: SetMarkingsEnabled(document.RID, true) synthesises a Rule{Type: RuleTypeMarkingSubset, ObjectProperty: MarkingField} inside compilePolicies — no explicit OBJECT-scope rules are attached so the auto clause is the only policy in play

sequence: For each userId in [alice, bob, carol]: svc.ListObjects(ctx{user=userId}, {ontology=marking_e2e, objectType=document, pageSize=50})
Collect returned WireObject.PrimaryKey values and assert the exact set matches the matrix expectation
request.policyEngine: pkg/security.Engine wired via svc.SetPolicyEngine, markings opt-in via svc.policyEngine.SetMarkingsEnabled

expected.semantics: auth.EvaluateMarkings(user, object) := object.markings ⊆ user.markings. Objects with an empty/nil _markings slice remain public. Single-valued marking overlap (the US-051 should-terms auto-clause) is not sufficient to enforce this and was the red bar for US-052
expected.rowCount: ListObjects.totalCount reflects Bleve's pre-subset total (the should-terms pass lets docBothRequired through for alice / bob), but ObjectPage.Data is post-filtered down to the subset-legal rows; future tightening may align totalCount with the post-pass count

ListObjects.data: []WireObject — each row exposes $primaryKey / $apiName / $rid plus the selected properties
ListObjects.totalCount: string — reflects the Bleve hit count after the AND-merged policy pre-filter. The post-Bleve applyMarkingFilter pass may drop additional rows from Data without decrementing totalCount

notes: Run with `go test -tags integration ./test/integration/... -run MarkingE2E`. Requires Docker for testcontainers.

`_markings` is a reserved keyword field on every ObjectType index — tests do not need to declare it in the schema Properties slice. Writers attach the slice through funnel.Edit.Markings (the explicit side-channel) rather than through Properties['_markings'] so ingest keeps markings as metadata.

The US-051 auto-marking compile path emits a BooleanQuery with MinShould=1, which is correct for single-valued marking fields but leaks docBothRequired to alice / bob when markings are multi-valued. US-052 resolves this with a post-Bleve verification pass (oss.ServiceImpl.applyMarkingFilter) that runs auth.EvaluateMarkings per row between applyPolicyFilter and applyPropertyVisibility. A future follow-up may fold a markings signature field into the index so subset can be expressed directly as a Bleve query, but the post-pass is sufficient for the US-052 acceptance bar.
applyMarkingFilter is a no-op unless the engine has SetMarkingsEnabled(ot.RID, true); un-opted object types never pay the per-row EvaluateMarkings cost.

The same applyMarkingFilter pass is also wired into GetObject, SearchObjects, and ListLinkedObjects so every OSS read path enforces the subset invariant consistently — US-052 only asserts ListObjects but the service-level hook guards the whole read surface.
